title: Snapchat Launches Easy Lens CLI, Supporting AI Assistants Such as Claude Code and Cursor in Building AR Filters
excerpt: On Wednesday, November 18, Snapchat announced the launch of Easy Lens CLI, allowing AR filter creators to directly invoke AI coding assistants such as Claude Co
content_html:
On Wednesday, November 18, Snapchat announced the launch of Easy Lens CLI, allowing AR filter creators to directly invoke AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex to build core special effects Lenses, aiming to lower the barrier to AR content creation and integrate the platform into developers' existing workflows.

The tool evolved from the Easy Lens tool, which generates filters from a single prompt on web and mobile, and supports Mac, Windows, and Linux. Creators only need to describe their requirements in natural language, and the AI assistant can independently complete end-to-end development: invoking more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, fixing errors, building tests, pushing updates to phones, and publishing tracking data. With this capability, Web Lens games with leaderboards, camera effects, and beauty filters can be developed with zero code, and games can be compressed from idea to launch in one day.

On the ecosystem and commercialization level, Snapchat did not force developers to learn proprietary tools; instead, it follows the trend of AI programming becoming more widespread, helping game developers convert browser games into web filters, making it easy for AI creators to reuse existing assets, and helping agencies and brands quickly convert promotional graphics, text, and videos into AR experiences. Creators participating in the paid Snapchat Lens+ program can create and monetize through this tool. The company disclosed that it paid $1.8 million to community creators last month.

Embedding AR development into mainstream AI programming environments helps expand Snapchat's developer base and reflects the industry trend of AI-assisted development extending from traditional software engineering to spatial computing and social AR effects.
